model_annotation: The image displays two distinct bar charts illustrating the share of GDP (% des BIP¹) contributed by different German administrative levels over time, with the left chart showing stacked bars and the right chart showing individual bars for comparison. In the left chart, the horizontal axis represents years from 1991 to 2023, while the vertical axis, labeled "% des BIP¹", ranges from -0.5 to 3.5 in linear increments. Each vertical bar is stacked into three colored segments: blue for "Bund" (federal level), purple for "Länder" (states), and green for "Gemeinden" (municipalities), representing their respective contributions to the total GDP share. The bars are sorted chronologically, and a vertical dashed line marks the year 2000, annotated with "Bahnhreform²". The tallest bars, around 1991, reach approximately 3.3% for the total, with the blue segment starting around 0.7%, the purple around 0.8%, and the green around 1.8%. The right chart uses the same horizontal axis and vertical scale but plots individual bars for each year, with the same color coding for "Bund", "Länder", and "Gemeinden", and overlays a black line labeled "Gebietskörperschaften insgesamt" (total territorial entities). This chart shows that the total contribution from all levels combined peaked around 1991 at approximately 0.9% before declining to near zero in subsequent years, with the black line showing a similar trend. Both charts visually emphasize the year 2000 with a dashed vertical line and annotation, and neither chart shows any bars with special visual emphasis beyond their color-coding and stacking arrangement.
